why_video_not_article.answer: The story depends on the viewer repeatedly seeing a physical laptop stand in for a human location, then watching one apparent employee split into multiple trust signals, then seeing the same physical infrastructure reverse from disguise into evidence. Those spatial, object-based and transformation ideas lose force when reduced to prose.

key_visual.concept: An ordinary company laptop sitting inside an ordinary American home while the human operator is visually separated from it by geography.
key_visual.role: The laptop is the persistent hero object and changes meaning eight times across the episode.

key_demonstration_or_diagram.concept: Device-location / human-location separation followed by employee-card decomposition into identity, interview, hosted laptop, actual work and payment/account.
key_demonstration_or_diagram.role: Turns an abstract trust problem into a visible system the viewer can understand in seconds.

potential: DOJ/FBI/IC3 evidence cards and public official releases
Official-source labels for current allegation vs proven case
archive_or_real_world_evidence.limitation: PP02 confirms evidence potential, not rights clearance. Actual visual-source/rights approval occurs at PP05.

editor_feasibility_note.assessment: The episode can be built predominantly from original illustration, map graphics, evidence cards, controlled typography and object-led motion. It does not require unverifiable crime-scene footage, expensive 3D, reenactment actors, or generic cyber stock to carry the story.
editor_feasibility_note.mitigation: Reserve more motion-design attention for the two reveal beats; all other shots are low-to-medium complexity.

why_video_proof.thesis: The viewer must see the mismatch between object, place and human—not merely be told it.

non_textual_information.visual_only_value: Normal house + real-looking work laptops creates the contradiction before explanation.
Keeping the device fixed in Nashville while moving the human elsewhere makes the case mechanism instantly legible.
Attaching a location pin to the laptop instead of the person produces the central mental model.
A map multiplying homes conveys distributed scale without a spoken statistics dump.
One employee card splitting across several actors makes identity modularity comprehensible.
Layered scale cards convert many figures into escalating consequence instead of report-like narration.
Reversing the same path visually turns disguise into evidence—a genuine visual reversal.
Keeping verification checks green while changing the human behind them creates the final conceptual payoff.

why_video_proof.article_failure_mode: As an article, the episode would rely on repeated explanations of device location, identity and trust signals. In video, those explanations are externalized into objects, maps and transformations, allowing narration to stay conversational and sparse.

evidence_strategy.separation_rule: Illustration must never masquerade as real evidence

expensive_or_risky: Rights-cleared real evidence may be limited; data-card fallback is acceptable if visually strong.

Final wrong-human reveal must feel elegant, not like a corporate infographic.
unnecessary_production: No real victim-company logo recreation required.
No North Korea history/military montage required.

participants.reason: Every movement has a distinct visual job and the story does not depend on spoken repetition.
41 shots are bounded; only one high-complexity reveal; no expensive reenactment/3D dependency.
Hero-object continuity supports coherent framing and callbacks.
Object-led, map-led and card-led language provides a strong base for art direction.
The visual transformations carry story progression, especially M03, M05, M07 and M08.
The structure contains clear silence/reveal/scale transitions for later sonic spotting without requiring music to manufacture drama.
